Summary

The course has a quality score of 62/100. Three of 8 ILOs have no assessment. The QM review found two critical problems in Module 4. idstack recommends that you add a rubric to the Module 4 project first.

Quality 62/100 · Accessibility 71/100 · Confidence 4/5

Findings

critical T1 Finding alignment-1: Module 4 has no rubric

What we saw
The Module 4 project asks learners to analyze a data set (module-04-project.md), but the course has no rubric for it.
What the evidence says
Rubrics with clear criteria improve self-assessment and performance (Panadero & Jonsson, 2013; Brookhart, 2018). [Assessment-8] [T1]
Why it matters
Without a rubric, learners do not know the criteria for a good result. Feedback is then less useful to them.
Recommendation
idstack recommends that you add a four-level analytic rubric. You can run /idstack:assessment-design to write one.

warning Finding cogload-2: Long video segments

What we saw
The course syllabus says: Each lecture video runs about 45 minutes; watch them all before the quiz.
What the evidence says
Short segments decrease extraneous cognitive load for novice learners, according to Mayer et al. (2019). [CogLoad-4] [CogLoad-19] [T1]
Recommendation
You can cut each video into parts of 6 to 10 minutes. WCAG 2.1 success criterion 1.2.2 also applies to these videos.

Finding access-3: Faculty text

What we saw
Students should utilize the discussion board; posts are graded weekly, and late posts won't count.

Top recommendations

  1. Add a rubric to the Module 4 project. [Assessment-8] [T1]
  2. Cut the lecture videos into short segments. [CogLoad-4] [T1]

Limitations

This review used only the manifest and the files in .idstack/course-content/. It did not examine the LMS gradebook.

Quoted policy text from the institution; it is not idstack text, so the checker skips it.

Next steps

  1. Run /idstack:assessment-design and write the Module 4 rubric.
  2. Run this skill again after you change the course.
